cases.title: Black robe
cases.semanticExcerpt: '''Black robe''' is one of the basic pieces of chest armour for low level [[Magic]] users. Black robes are often dropped by the [[dark wizard]]s in the stone circle south of [[Varrock]]. It has identical stats to the [[blue wizard robe]], as well as its [[Black wizard robe (t)|trimmed]] and [[Black wizard robe (g)|gold-trimmed]] versions. It can be created by using [[black dye]] on a blue wizard robe; similarly, it can also be turned into a blue wizard robe by using [[blue dye]] on it.
secondaryExcerpts: The black robe is often worn with the black [[wizard hat]] and [[black skirt]] for aesthetics. The hat has a slightly darker tone than the robes, instead more closely matching the [[priest gown]]. This is not the case with the robe's trimmed versions.

One of only three [[Body slot table (F2P)|free-to-play bodies]] with a magic attack bonus, the Black robe, [[Blue wizard robe]], and their [[Ornamental armour|ornamental variants]] get +1 [[Magic]] attack and -3 [[Prayer]] bonus compared to the [[Zamorak monk top]].

cases.title: Dragon longsword
cases.semanticExcerpt: '''dragon longsword''' is the third-strongest [[longsword]] available in ''[[Old School RuneScape]]'', and can only be wielded by players who have at least 60 [[Attack]] and have completed the [[Lost City]] quest.
secondaryExcerpts: As with all [[dragon weapons]], players cannot make this item using the [[Smithing]] skill. However, it can be purchased in the [[Zanaris#Market area|Zanaris marketplace]] from [[Jukat]] for 100,000 coins (requires a [[Diamond]] for entry). The weapon can also be received as a reward from elite [[Treasure Trails]].

It is a preferred weapon for players buying their first dragon weapon as it has a low cost but can still inflict significant damage. For a long time, prior to the 2005 introduction of the [[abyssal whip]] and [[dragon scimitar]], this was the weapon of choice for both [[player killing]] and training.

It can be upgraded to the [[Dragon longsword (bh)]] with a [[Dragon longsword imbue scroll]], which has a +4 increased stab and +6 slash attack bonus, and a +25% accuracy bonus to the special attack. In addition, the special attack consumes only 15% special attack energy rather than 25%, and is one [[tick]] faster (2.4 seconds instead of 3.0 seconds). The upgraded version can only be used for [[PKing]] in the [[Bounty Hunter]] [[Minigames|minigame.]]

==Special attack==
[[File:The Judgement.gif|frame|A player uses ''The Judgement'', the Armadyl godsword's special attack]]
Like all godswords, the Armadyl godsword has a [[special attacks|special attack]], ''The Judgement'', which consumes 50% of the player's special attack energy. In addition to doubled accuracy, its max hit is boosted twice: first by the hidden 1.1x multiplier every godsword special possesses (rounded down to an integer), then by a further 1.25x on top of that, giving a combined ~37.5% increase over its normal max hit. ''The Judgement'' also always rolls against the opponent's slash defence roll.

''The Judgement'' is capable of dealing a very large amount of damage; under ideal conditions, a player can potentially deal over 70 damage to a [[monster]] with the special attack, or just over 90 damage when utilising the effects of a [[black mask]] or a [[Castle wars bracelet]]. Because of this, the Armadyl godsword is very popular for many combat situations. In PvP scenarios the Armadyl godsword is most commonly used as a "knock-out" weapon, as the special is often capable of finishing an injured player in one large blow. In PvM scenarios its high hits are advantageous when fighting [[boss]] monsters such as [[General Graardor]], especially when several players are competing to deal the most damage in order to secure a drop.

The special attack [[animation]]'s colours can be changed to gold, which costs 75 [[Last Man Standing]] points. Once unlocked, the gold trim can be toggled at [[Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing]] whenever the player desires.

secondaryExcerpts: When worn, all drops received from [[Non-player character|NPCs]] within the [[Revenant Caves]], [[Wilderness Slayer Cave]] and [[Chaos Temple (Wilderness)|Chaos Temple]] will be in the form of [[bank note]]s, except for secondary supply rolls and uniques. However, equipping the amulet will cause the player to become [[Skull (status)|skulled]], similar to the [[cape of skulls]]. Attempting to equip the amulet gives a warning telling the player that this will happen. The skull cannot be removed until the amulet is unequipped, after which it behaves like a normal PK skull and disappears after twenty minutes. This behaviour is different from the [[cape of skulls]], which will only keep the skull active for 20 minutes from the moment of equipping.

If the amulet is worn while killing the [[Revenant maledictus]] as a top-damaging player, they will obtain the [[Forinthry surge|Forinthry Surge]] skull for 30 minutes, a variant that provides an additional 15% accuracy and damage boost when fighting revenants. Taking off the amulet will automatically remove this buff.

cases.title: Bow of Faerdhinen (c)
cases.semanticExcerpt: '''bow of Faerdhinen (c)''' is a corrupted version of the [[Bow of Faerdhinen]] that does not [[Degradation|degrade]], with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the [[Corrupted Gauntlet]]. The bow's colours may be changed to other colours of the [[Elven Clans]] by buying crystals from [[Lliann's Wares]] in [[Prifddinas]], which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the [[crystal of Hefin]] on any variant of the corrupted bow.
secondaryExcerpts: The bow can be upgraded by bringing it and 2,000 [[crystal shard]]s to a [[singing bowl]]. Doing so requires level 82 [[Smithing]] and [[Crafting]] (the levels can be [[Temporary skill boost|boosted]]), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have [[Conwenna]] or [[Reese]] sing the crystal in their stead for an extra 1,000 crystal shards. Excess charges in the bow will be taken into account; for example, a newly created bow with 10,000 charges will require 1,900 crystal shards to corrupt and a fully charged bow will only cost 1,800 crystal shards to upgrade.

Alternatively, the [[Bow of Faerdhinen]] can be corrupted passively through use: every 100 shots fired from the bow contributes 1 shard worth of progress toward the 1,900-shard corruption requirement. Once this cumulative amount is reached, the bow can be corrupted at the singing bowl with the level requirements or have Conwenna corrupt it for you for the 1000 shard price. Any combination of progress towards corruption, charges in the bow, and crystal shards can be used to meet the crystal shard requirement to corrupt the bow.
While untradeable, the bow can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will '''not''' be returned.

Like its regular variant, the bow requires level 80 [[Ranged]] and 70 [[Agility]] to wield, and provides the highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus out of any weapon for its [[attack speed]]. It also benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when [[crystal armour]] is equipped. Each [[crystal armour]] piece equipped grants additional bonus accuracy and damage, adding up to a total 15% damage and 30% accuracy bonus when the full set is equipped.

When using crystal armour, the bow provides similar damage per second to the [[twisted bow]] and [[toxic blowpipe]]; however, these weapons excel against targets with high Magic level and low Defence respectively. Unlike the twisted bow or toxic blowpipe, the corrupted bow of Faerdhinen suffers no significant drawback and provides consistent performance due to its high accuracy and damage per shot, along with its moderate attack speed, long range, and unlimited ammunition.
